items.label: text
items.text: High-density poly(ethene) is used where greater strength and rigidity are needed, for example to make plastic bottles such as milk bottles. If you can find a recycling symbol with the letters HDPE next to it, then the bottle is made of high-density poly(ethene). If it has some other letters there, then it is made of a different polymer.

items.text: HOW TO DEDUCE THE POLYMERISATION REACTION FOR ANY ALKENE

items.label: text
items.text: Figure 29.6 shows how to work out a polymerisation reaction starting from any alkene. The key thing is to always draw the alkene as shown with just the C=C in the middle.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 29.6 How to work out a polymerisation reaction

items.label: text
items.text: Propene is another alkene, this time with three carbon atoms in each molecule. Its formula is normally written as CH3CH=CH. Think of it as a modified ethene molecule, with a CH3 group attached in place of one of the hydrogen atoms.

items.label: text
items.text: When propene is polymerised you obtain poly(propene). This used to be called polypropylene.
